title: How to Capture HTTP Headers (HAR file) on the Client System

blocks.text: The method to capture HTTP headers depends on how an end user accesses the website or the web application.

blocks.heading: The Website or Web Application Is Accessed from an Internet Browser

blocks.text: In this case, the most efficient method is to use the developer tools option available on most modern browsers.
Click one of the following options to read the relevant instructions:
The following sections provide detailed instructions on how to export complete HAR traces from latest Chromium-based browsers.

Chromium versions 130 and later limit the level of detail in the exported HAR file. For more information, refer to the Google Release Notes. Although this level of detail is generally sufficient for most issues, you might want to capture all the HTTP data when debugging certain issues related to authentication or session-related errors, POST request failures, API debugging, or some complex interactions with third-party scripts or ads.
To capture all data in the exported HAR file, you must first adjust the settings in Developer Tools:

blocks.item: Click the Settings icon in the top right corner.
Scroll down until you see the Network section and select the box Allow to generate HAR (with sensitive data).
Click and hold Export until a menu appears with the option to export sensitive data.

blocks.heading: A Thick Application Is Required for Access

blocks.text: For such non-browser applications (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Slack), you need a third-party application such as Fiddler or Charles Proxy to capture the HTTP headers. These applications insert themselves as the system proxy to intercept and capture the web traffic.
Select one of the following options to read the relevant instructions for Fiddler.

blocks.heading: Zscaler Client Connector Is Not Enabled on the System

blocks.text: If Zscaler Client Connector is not enabled on the system:

blocks.item: Install Fiddler Classic. To perform a Fiddler capture, you must have Fiddler installed on the user machine. Download Fiddler Classic from the official website.
Launch Fiddler Classic. After Fiddler Classic is installed, launch it from the Start menu.

Configure Fiddler Classic. Enable HTTPS decryption by going to Tools > Options > HTTPS and enabling the Decrypt HTTPS traffic checkbox. Click Yes to install and trust the Fiddler Classic Root certificate.
Start the Fiddler capture. Click the File menu and ensure that the Capture Traffic option is enabled.
Reproduce the problem. With Fiddler capturing the traffic, you can request the user to re-create the problem. At the same time, check whether Fiddler is capturing the live web traffic.
Save the capture. Go to File menu > Save > All sessions to save the capture as *.saz file.

blocks.heading: Zscaler Client Connector Is Enabled on the System

blocks.text: For instructions on what to do if Zscaler Client Connector is enabled on the system, see Using Fiddler with Zscaler Client Connector.
